headword: {一味唐辛子|いちみとうがらし}

definitions.gloss: ground red chili pepper; cayenne pepper
definitions.explanation: A single-ingredient spice made from dried and ground red chili peppers. A standard condiment on Japanese dining tables, used to add heat to noodles, grilled dishes, and more.

examples.japanese: うどんに{一味唐辛子|いちみとうがらし}をかける。
examples.english: To sprinkle ground chili pepper on udon.

examples.japanese: {一味唐辛子|いちみとうがらし}を{少|すこ}し{入|い}れると{味|あじ}が{引|し}き{締|し}まる。
examples.english: Adding a little ground chili pepper tightens up the flavor.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}では{一味唐辛子|いちみとうがらし}と{七味唐辛子|しちみとうがらし}の{両方|りょうほう}がテーブルに{置|お}いてある。
examples.english: At this restaurant, both ground chili pepper and seven-spice blend are available on the table.

notes: Literally 'one-flavor chili pepper,' meaning it contains only chili pepper with no other spices mixed in. Contrast with {七味唐辛子|しちみとうがらし} (seven-spice chili blend), which combines chili with ingredients like {山椒|さんしょう} (Japanese pepper), {陳皮|ちんぴ} (dried citrus peel), and sesame. Often shortened to {一味|いちみ} in casual speech. A staple condiment at {蕎麦|そば} and udon restaurants.
